article_text:
讀者投稿／王崢 劇照提供／東京國際電影節 責任編輯／黃曦 核稿編輯／黃曦

如果說過去十年有所謂「東北文藝復興」，那麼它最成功的地方，或許並非重新呈示雪、工廠、下崗工人和九〇年代，而是讓一批本來已經退出歷史敘事的人，再次回返與言說。

以雙雪濤、班宇、鄭執為中心的新東北文學，雙雪濤出版於 2016 年的小說《平原上的摩西》，後由張大磊執導、改編為同名劇集，該作亦於童年入選柏林影展聚集單元；由辛爽執導、發表於 2023 年的劇集《漫長的季節》雖非直接改編班宇的同名小說，不過班宇仍作為該劇文學策劃，且劇中角色寫就的詩歌〈漫長的〉也同樣出自班宇作品。

與文學系譜緊密相連的地方歷史、祖輩記憶，評論家金赫楠談及《平原上的摩西》時，曾提出一道重要的判斷：法律可以確知一個人是否有罪，但小說的工作並非要重新破案，而是讓受害者、嫌疑人與旁觀者，重新進入人情、人性與歷史的尺度。

因此，「真正的小說家在面對自己的人物，總是理解先於審判」。 換句話說，在法律審判結束之後，文學偷偷搭建了另一個法庭，它未必推翻判決，卻可以重新分配罪責和理解：一個人在法律上有罪，不代表歷史便是無罪；一個人有／沒有犯法，也不代表他是否被時代所傷。

《我的朋友安德烈》電影劇照／劇照提供：東京國際電影節

由董子健執導、偕同劉昊然主演，改編自雙雪濤同名小說的《我的朋友安德烈》（My Friend Andrei），不同於雙雪濤的其他犯罪小說及其改編，《我的朋友安德烈》甚至取消了「法庭」所需要的案件。

在 2024 年於第 37 屆東京國際電影節主競賽單元進行世界首映後，董子健提到原著小說使他產生強烈的「懷舊感」，也讓他意識到「成為一個完整的人」本身，可能是痛苦的。 因而，這不是另一本《平原上的摩西》，沒有殺人案等待偵破，沒有兇手等待裁決，真正需要被「重審」的，是回到東北家鄉、參加父親葬禮的李默，他的一生終旋繞著如此的疑問：他為什麼活下來，為什麼離開？又為什麼成功長大，且必須忘掉那個，沒有成功長大的朋友？

《我的朋友安德烈》電影最激進、也最冒險的改編，就發生在安德烈身上。在雙雪濤小說裡的安德烈並沒有死亡，他成年後精神失常，最終被送進精神病院；電影把「安德烈之瘋」改成「安德烈之死」，或者說，至少看起來是這樣：少年安德烈因替李默揭發成績遭篡改，在父親暴打之下意外被滾燙的開水燙死；目睹一切的李默此後產生幻覺，心理之痛甚至變成身體上無法解釋的痛癢。

於是，成年董子健所飾演的安德烈，從一開始就不真正屬於現實。他坐在李默旁邊，和他乘車、說話、爭吵，看起來比誰都具體，實際上卻是被記憶召回的亡靈。 原著讓李默面對一個「還活著卻已經被生活摧毀的人」，電影則更殘酷地逼使李默承認，他的朋友沒有機會繼續長大。

《我的朋友安德烈》電影劇照／劇照提供：東京國際電影節

墨西哥作家克里斯蒂娜・里維拉・加爾薩（Cristina Rivera Garza）提出的「亡靈寫作」（Necro-Writing），意指在暴力、掠奪與抹除之後，重新與無法自行言說的人，共同寫作。因此，它甚至可能成為一種，對抗遺忘、重新確認生命的行為。

《我的朋友安德烈》最漂亮的地方，即是將這樣的亡靈意義，自角色擴延至整個東北。比如，兩個孩子曾在廢棄舊工廠奔跑、嬉鬧，而成年李默再次見到童年的安德烈時，工廠已經成為一具巨大的工業屍體。 人死了，工廠也死了，少年時代死了，父輩相信的秩序也死了。安德烈不只是一個死去的朋友，他幾乎就是那個消失世界的人形殘影。

當李默的背開始莫名發癢，甚至感受到猶如安德烈被燙傷的痛楚時，曾經的痛癢不只是存在於記憶之中，而成為了一種活物。因為亡靈沒有肉身，只好借你的皮膚繼續疼痛。 貫穿電影和原著的重要隱喻和線索，足球是李默與安德烈成為朋友的契機，自雪花到足球的借喻，也讓被凍結的年少時代，成為重新滾動起來的記憶。本應不斷向前滾動的足球，反觀永遠停在年少時代的安德烈，愈是輕盈的球，也愈是襯映出沒有抵達的明天。

《我的朋友安德烈》電影劇照／劇照提供：東京國際電影節

然而，這也是我對電影最矛盾，卻最喜歡它的地方。《北京青年報》的評論家余小魚，批評《我的朋友安德烈》電影與原著之間，有著根本性的斷裂： 小說努力追問人物困境背後的時代因果，電影卻抽空了不少具體社會關係，最後退回「私人創傷的悼念與懷念」。

這個批評並非沒有道理，學費、階級、教師權力、家庭暴力、工廠衰敗，本來都是可以繼續向下挖掘的現實，但電影卻用一次次的大雪、廢墟、幻覺和身體症狀將之作為象徵。 電影裡大量使用的空鏡轉場、固定鏡頭，形成極端的風格化呈現，這的確是導演過分清楚什麼時候應作隱喻，致使觀眾也難以真正思及鐵鏽、油污與汗漬的東北。

不過，若是將風格化詮釋為對「真實」的損耗，也可能低估《我的朋友安德烈》在電影技術上的完成度。這部片真正可看之處未必是演員，而是幕後團隊：攝影指導呂松野、剪輯張叔平、聲音指導李丹楓、原創音樂李衡。

呂松野的攝影尤其適合「亡靈」的故事。電影大量使用固定鏡頭、空景，不讓攝影機直直追隨人物，也不總是靠近臉部捕捉情緒，而更接近一種將人物安置在一個已經存在，甚至比人物更長壽的空間裡。

因而工廠、雪地、走廊和門也不再只是「背景」，能逐漸取得與人物相同的敘事重量。比如，成年李默與安德烈在郊外酒店對坐時，一棵發出冷光的聖誕樹正好將兩人置於構圖兩端；父親工作過的廠房，則由沉重鐵門構成凝滯的空間。

亦即，真正重要的不是角色佔據多少畫面，而是他周圍有多少空白、多少無法穿越的空間。這也解釋了成年安德烈明明「出現在鏡頭裡」，觀眾卻始終感覺他並不完全存在── 他和活人站在同一個景深裡，卻像被整個空間悄悄排除在現實之外，而這樣的處理更加接近亡靈的意義，亡靈僅僅作為一直在場，卻沒有辦法再次／重新進入時間、被時間記述之物。

《我的朋友安德烈》電影劇照／劇照提供：東京國際電影節

另一方面，電影透過反覆交錯成年、少年時空的剪輯結構，呈現出現在與未來彼此滲透的非線性時間意義：透過創傷、感受、物件或空間而發生鏡頭之間的關係，其次才因信興時間的故事因果而產生關係。

於是，觀眾將在接受成年安德烈的存在之後，才慢慢意識到其存在本身的問題所在。 換句話說，電影並不透過剪輯處理、爬梳李默的記憶，而是藉由呈現「創傷」與「記憶」本身的特性──省略（Ellipsis）、重返、錯置、延遲──最終延展出完整的故事網絡。

也許，《我的朋友安德烈》的成功偏偏就在這樣的失真中，《平原上的摩西》讓文學在法律之外進行第二次審判；《我的朋友安德烈》則在死亡之後進行第二次解放。

但安德烈可以成為周旋於李默的亡靈，他反而第一次獲得絕對自由。他可以出現在飛機上，可以走進雪地，可以重新回到工廠，可以質問那個活下來、離開東北、學會遺忘的朋友。 唯有文學和電影才能完成的，是一個已死之人，能夠回來要活著的人，繼續、重新記憶他。

所以《我的朋友安德烈》真正要埋葬的，從來不是安德烈。在大雪覆蓋工廠、道路和少年時代，李默得到的是遲到了幾十年的自由，他或許終能承認，有些人之所以必須變成亡靈，是因為只有死者，才有能力穿過我們為自己築起的一切辯解。
excerpt_original: 《我的朋友安德烈》最漂亮的地方，即是將「亡靈寫作」（Necro-Writing）的意義，自角色擴延至整個東北。兩個孩子曾在廢棄舊工廠奔跑、嬉鬧，到成年李默再次見到童年的安德烈時，工廠已經成為巨大的工業屍體。人死了，工廠也死了，少年時代死了，父輩相信的秩序也死了，安德烈幾乎就是那個消失世界的人形殘影。 這篇文章 《我的朋友安德烈》：生者與亡靈的寫作 最早出現於 釀電影 。

article_text:
Hollywood director Michael Mann has been taken to the hospital following an apparently accidental shooting at a Los Angeles gun range, according to the Associated Press.

Mann, 83, reportedly shot himself in the leg while at the The Range LA. The news was first reported on celebrity website TMZ. He sustained what his representative described as a superficial injury after a weapon accidentally discharged while holstered.

Mann is one of the best known long-standing directors in Hollywood, known for major works like Manhunter, The Last of the Mohicans and Heat. His most recent move was Ferrari, starring Adam Driver and Penelope Cruz, that was released in 2023. Mann also helped created the hit 1980s TV cop show Miami Vice.

TMZ reported that Mann had been trying to holster his weapon when the gun accidentally discharged. Emergency services were then called and he was taken to a hospital.

Mann is preparing to shoot a sequel to Heat – one of the most acclaimed crime move of recent decades – starring Christian Bale and Leonardo DiCaprio.

Michael Mann

Los Angeles

article_text:
京都産業大学ギャラリー（京都市下京区）で、「南蛮―異文化が交差した京都の記憶―」が11月2日から12月12日まで開催されます。入場無料。

16世紀中頃から17世紀にかけて来航したポルトガル人やスペイン人らヨーロッパ人は「南蛮人」と呼ばれ、鉄砲をはじめとするさまざまな文物を日本にもたらしました。キリスト教もその一つで、天文18年（1549年）にフランシスコ・ザビエルが来日して以降、宣教師たちは各地で布教活動を展開します。天正4年（1576年）、京都・四条坊門姥柳町にて献堂式が行われた「被昇天の聖母教会」は、「都の南蛮寺」として広く知られていましたが、宗教と弾圧が進むなかでその姿を消してしまいました。令和8年（2026年）は、「都の南蛮寺」の献堂から450年にあたります。

本展では、かつて南蛮寺が建てられるなど異文化受容の要所でもあった京都を舞台に、当時の人々の異国への眼差しや信仰、工芸技術の交流を多彩な資料からたどります。

南蛮―異文化が交差した京都の記憶―

詳細は、 京都産業大学ギャラリー公式サイト まで。

本展の見どころと注目作品

南蛮文化館蔵《南蛮屏風》を公開

南蛮文化館（大阪市中津）が所蔵する代表的な名品《南蛮屏風》の右隻が展示されます。本展では右隻のみの展示となりますが、左隻は本展と同時期の11月に、南蛮文化館にて展示される予定です。（11/1～30まで）

東西の文化が交錯する港や異国情緒あふれる人々の賑わいを描いた名品を、両館を巡り、あわせて楽しむことができる特別な機会となります。南蛮文化館の詳細については、同館の 公式サイト をご確認ください。

東西の信仰と技術が交差する工芸と出土資料

キリスト教の伝来とともに制作された優美な漆工芸品《イエズス会紋章入り書見台》や、京都の地でキリシタン信仰が確かに息づいていた歴史を物語る「京都南蛮寺出土人物線刻硯」など、信仰と卓越した日本の伝統工芸が融合した貴重な作品・資料が紹介されます。細密な螺鈿と蒔絵によるイエズス会の紋章意匠、そして発掘調査で出土したものや、伝世品から、当時の熱気あふれる東西交流の一端を肌で感じ取ることができます。

京都産業大学ギャラリー（むすびわざ館）とは

京都産業大学ギャラリーは、2012年に開設された「むすびわざ館」内に位置し、大学の研究成果や貴重な所蔵資料、地域と連携した文化財などを広く一般に公開・発信する教育研究施設です。文化・学術の結節点として、京都の歴史・伝統文化など多彩なテーマの企画展や特別展が開催されています。

16世紀末から17世紀初頭にかけて日本列島を席巻した南蛮文化。異国の風を真っ先に受け止め、新たな造形美へと昇華させた当時の息吹は、今なお色あせることのない鮮烈な輝きを放っています。秋が深まる京都の地で、かつて都の人々を魅了したエキゾチックな美と信仰の歴史に思いを馳せてみてはいかがでしょうか。同時期に大阪の南蛮文化館で公開される《南蛮屏風》左隻とあわせて見ることで、屏風に描かれた雄大な世界観をより深く堪能できそうです。（美術展ナビ）

Novo “X-Men” tem estreia prevista para 5 de maio de 2028.

Um novo mutante se junta ao Instituto Xavier. O ator Asa Germann se juntou ao elenco do novo “ X-Men ” no papel de Warren Worthington III, mais conhecido como Anjo (via THR ).

Germann é mais conhecido por seu trabalho nas séries “Gen V” e “The Boys”, onde interpretava o jovem super Sam Riordan, um dos aliados do Capitão Pátria na Universidade Godolkin. Ele também esteve em “Pânico 7” recentemente, no papel de Lucas Bowen. Segundo o relato, Germann fez testes para o papel de Scott Summers, o Ciclope, em “X-Men”, mas foi escolhido para o papel do Anjo.

O Anjo foi criado por Stan Lee e Jack Kirby, sendo apresentado logo na primeira edição de “X-Men” em 1963. Sua mutação consiste em asas emplumadas nas costas que lhe permitem voar. Em certo momento de sua trajetória, o Anjo foi mutilado e teve suas asas substituídas por asas metálicas capazes de disparar projéteis, uma alteração feita pelo vilão Apocalipse. Nos cinemas, o personagem foi vivido por Ben Foster em “X-Men: O Confronto Final” e Ben Hardy em “X-Men: Apocalipse”.

Germann se junta ao elenco que já conta com Sadie Sink como Jean Grey, Kit Connor como o Ciclope, Inde Navarrette como a Vampira, Maya Boyd como a Tempestade e Christopher Abbott como Charles Xavier, o Professor X. Entre os vilões, Samara Weaving será Emma Frost, com Adam Driver interpretando Nathaniel Milbury, o Sr. Sinistro.

Jake Schreier assume a direção do novo “X-Men” após o sucesso de “Thunderbolts*”. O roteiro fica a cargo de Lee Sung Jin, que já trabalhou com Schreier na série “Beef”, e de Joanna Calo.

O novo “X-Men” tem estreia prevista para 5 de maio de 2028.

article_text:
California lawmakers began a discussion Thursday about removing the cap on the state’s $750 million incentive for film and TV production, while acknowledging that such a move would face budget hurdles.

At an Assembly committee hearing in North Hollywood, a handful of state lawmakers heard testimony from union leaders and industry advocates who argued that the program — which was doubled last year — is not enough to stop the outflow of production jobs.

Betsy Beers, the creative partner of Shonda Rhimes, told the committee that she had hoped to shoot a new “Grey’s Anatomy” spinoff in Santa Clarita. But the show, which is set in West Texas, did not get a California tax credit.

“We lost a lot of time, and a lot of money, and now we are filming in Albuquerque,” Beers said. “We want to be here.”

Because the state incentive is capped, projects must apply during periodic windows and then compete with other shows on a “jobs ratio” score. Beers said the show lost out initially because it didn’t get score highly enough. When ABC tried again in the fall, the program was already oversubscribed and was no longer taking applications.

“The program is still not competitive or predicable enough to address the loss of production to other regions,” said Arlen Valdivia, vice president of state government affairs at the Motion Picture Association. “There needs to be more done to make California competitive.”

FilmLA, the permitting agency, reported last week that production volume continues to fall in the Los Angeles area, even as the share of scripted TV shows receiving a state subsidy has nearly doubled. Several speakers at Thursday’s hearing called for eliminating the $750 million cap entirely — saying the limit leaves producers uncertain about whether they will get the credit.

Georgia’s credit has no limit and New York’s allows the state to pull from allocations for future years — amounting to an uncapped credit. Rick Chavez Zbur , who chairs the Assembly Select Committee on Growing and Retaining the Creative Economy in California, said he expects to make improvements in the next legislative session.

“I want to try to do our best to make whatever changes we can, and I think either increasing the cap or eliminating it,” Zbur said after the hearing. “But you know that is a heavy lift. But we’re going to try this year to make as much progress as we can.”

Lawmakers are also dealing with a structural deficit and deep cuts to Medicaid — which has intensified competition for tax dollars.

During the hearing, Zbur floated the idea of “dynamic scoring” — suggesting that the state should account for the benefit from the film credit instead just looking at the headline cost. That idea, he said, would be key to persuading lawmakers that an unlimited credit is a worthwhile investment.

“The way we’re looking at the return needs to be what we’re focused on,” said John Harabedian, another member of the committee. “It becomes a regional fight. It becomes a best-use-of-a-dollar fight… The numbers are going to convince our colleagues that don’t necessarily live in L.A.”

Rowan Isaaks, an economist with the state Legislative Analyst’s Office, cited research showing that film credits return 20-50 cents for every dollar invested by the state. He also expressed skepticism about dynamic scoring. “It’s subject to a lot of uncertainty,” he said.

Stephen Cheung, the president of the Los Angeles Economic Development Committee, cited his own group’s research, which found a return of $1.07 to state and local coffers. That report was funded by the MPA.

Assemblyman Nick Schultz floated the idea of extending the expiration date of the state program, which is currently set to sunset in 2030, as a way of offering greater certainty to productions. He and other also suggested providing a subsidy for above-the-line costs — salaries for actors, directors, etc. — and opening up eligibility for the program to commercials and game shows.

“Why should we be picking and choosing?” he asked. “Why should we be picking winners and losers? Let’s incentivize all of it to stay.”

The state raised the base credit from 20% to 35% last year, while increasing the overall cap from $330 million to $750 million.

“The higher credit might mean fewer projects overall,” Isaaks noted. “There’s a possibility that the more generous our credit is, the fewer productions we can fund in total.”

Since Gov. Gavin Newsom expanded the state incentive last year, lawmakers have added additional measures to bolster it. The Legislature created a $10 million incentive for post-production and passed a bill to expedite studio rebates and exempt credits for independent films from a $5 million credit cap.

While Congress is considering a 20% nationwide incentive, several speakers argued that even if that passes, California will still face stiff competition from other states.

“We should not assume the work will return because federal policy changes,” said Lindsay Dougherty, leader of the Hollywood Teamsters.

editorial_excerpt_zh: 作为当代艺术中的主导人物，辛迪·舍曼与大卫·萨利都是1970年代中期至80年代纽约颇具影响力的“图像一代”艺术运动的关键人物。在这个媒体主导的时代崭露头角，舍曼和萨利与许多同代人一样……
editorial_blocks_json: [{"type": "paragraph", "text": "档案——2016年10月20日", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "作为当代艺术中的主导人物，辛迪·舍曼与大卫·萨利都是1970年代中期至80年代纽约颇具影响力的“图像一代”艺术运动的关键人物。在这个媒体主导的时代崭露头角，舍曼和萨利与许多同代人一样，以现存的图像为灵感，创作出层次丰富的作品。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "大卫·萨利的《挂毯绘画》于1989年在伦敦沃丁顿画廊首次展出，并于1991年在纽约高古轩画廊展出，是对十六、十七世纪意大利和荷兰风俗风格的拼贴戏仿。背景图像取自历史挂毯中的叙事场景，其中一些是名作的复制品，另一些则出自一位匿名的俄罗斯挂毯制作者之手——萨利在一本杂志上看到其复制品，并将其临摹到画布上。这组作品展现出丰富的意象与构图的复杂性，是萨利最成熟的作品之一。部分《挂毯绘画》曾入选萨利作品的巡回回顾展，该展于1999年在阿姆斯特丹市立博物馆首展，但这一关键系列中的画作此后便再未展出。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "《挂毯绘画》以宏大的尺幅呈现，呼应历史挂毯的纪念碑式比例，却摒弃了其素材来源的叙事倾向，转而展现出风格的并置。淡雅的浅色背景刻意带有洛可可风格，画布中嵌入较小的灰色单色画与彩色图案。这些多层图像被赋予节奏与速度感，观者的目光在画面表面来回聚焦、失焦，从而将其提炼出来。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "在这组独特的作品中，萨利消解了叙事惯例，转而通过融入家具的装饰性图像、非洲面具的绘画图像以及贾科梅蒂雕塑等元素，在艺术史参照与各体裁之间建立对话。充满碰撞意象的《挂毯绘画》呈现出视觉上的喧闹，强调了观看的首要性。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "辛迪·舍曼的《历史肖像》同样在风格参照上直白显露，其灵感来自文艺复兴、巴洛克、洛可可和新古典主义时期的贵族历史画。舍曼直接受拉斐尔、卡拉瓦乔、安格尔和鲁本斯等人的肖像画启发，在古典构图的图像中使用一系列道具和服装，刻意迎合主观肖像画的陈词滥调。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "在贯穿其大量作品的创作中，舍曼同时扮演模特与图像创作者的角色。她采用不同的风格与人格，戏仿艺术中所描绘、媒体中所传播的女性刻板印象。通过使用道具和明显的假体身体部位，舍曼将注意力引向其作品的表演性，从而质疑这些归于男性的性别刻板印象的有效性。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "舍曼受邀与法国利摩日瓷器厂合作，创作了若干图像，尤其是1988年的《无题 #183》，大致以蓬帕杜夫人为原型。延续对人物的研究，舍曼创作了《女公民》《男公民》系列，于1989年法国大革命周年之际在巴黎展出。在罗马长期逗留期间，她拓展了这一主题，依据文艺复兴绘画创作了13幅肖像，并于1990年在纽约大都会图片社与法国系列一同展出。舍曼最终创作了第三个历史肖像系列，灵感主要来自文艺复兴和十七世纪。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "舍曼的重新诠释唤起绘画艺术，充满戏剧性与人工雕琢，质疑艺术史中再现的本质以及画家与模特之间的关系。舍曼每幅肖像的内在组成部分是其华丽的金色画框，她设计这些画框以强调每件作品中的绘画参照。这些照片的光泽表面与饱和色彩凸显了舍曼构图的人为性，强化了框内表演的戏剧性。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "表演主题同样是萨利作品的核心。萨利长期参与戏剧，与编舞家卡罗尔·阿米蒂奇合作超过25年，为她的芭蕾舞剧和歌剧设计布景与服装。早于他1992年融合绘画、摄影与表演的开创性《幽灵绘画》，《挂毯绘画》通过嵌入舞者绘画和其本人舞台摄影的照片转印图像，展现了跨文化的表演性影响对萨利作品的作用。这些大型绘画将意象与文化参照并置，本身就是编排好的表演，其画面成为萨利持续探索绘画表演性的舞台。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "在《历史肖像》中，舍曼从物理与概念两个层面以多层手法探索传统绘画体裁。构成肖像背景的厚重垂坠织物，以及照片表面浓郁密集的色彩，为她对这一历史体裁的挪用赋予实体形式。而在萨利的《挂毯绘画》中，来自艺术与设计史的众多引用层层叠加，成倍增加了可能的解读，并提供了一种另类的作者观念。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "展览将这两组作品置于对话之中，探讨两位艺术家作品中共享的视觉策略与内在的表演性。创作于同一时期的《历史肖像》与《挂毯绘画》邀请我们思考：在当代艺术史的这一特定时刻，两位艺术家对历史素材的共同转译何以不谋而合；也邀请我们审视他们各自所选的绘画与摄影媒介所扮演的角色。Sherman 与 Salle 借用视觉模式与风格，创造出层次丰富、原创而富有创造力的拼贴，这凸显了他们艺术造诣的成功，也凸显了这些历史性作品作为当代思想与实践之语境所具有的持续重要性。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Cindy Sherman and David Salle: History Portraits and Tapestry Paintings 2016年10月1日 – 11月26日 Skarstedt London Gallery 8 Bennet St London SW1A 1RP England http://www.skarstedt.com/", "translated": true}]

article_text:
Archives – October 20, 2016

Dominant figures in contemporary art, both Cindy Sherman and David Salle were key figures in the influential ‘Pictures Generation’ art movement of the mid 1970s and 80s in New York. Emerging onto the art scene during this media-dominated era, both Sherman and Salle, like many of their contemporaries, drew upon existing imagery as inspiration for their own richly layered work.

First exhibited in London at Waddington Galleries in 1989 and Gagosian Gallery, New York in 1991, David Salle’s Tapestry Paintings are a pastiche on sixteenth and seventeenth-century Italian and Dutch genre styles. The background imagery is drawn from narrative scenes from historical tapestries, some of which are reproductions of famous works, others are by an anonymous Russian tapestry-maker, which Salle found reproduced in a magazine and copied onto canvas. Demonstrating a richness of imagery and compositional complexity, this body of work is one of Salle’s most accomplished. A select number of Tapestry Paintings were included in the touring retrospective of Salle’s work, which originated at the Stedelijk Museum, Amsterdam in 1999, though paintings from this pivotal series have not been exhibited since.

Presented on a grand scale, in a nod to the monumental proportions of historical tapestries, the Tapestry Paintings eschew the narrative tendencies of their source material, demonstrating instead a simultaneity of styles. Delicately tinted, the pale backgrounds are deliberately rococo, with smaller grisaille paintings and colored motifs inset into the canvas. The multi-layered images are instilled with rhythm and velocity, which the eye distills as it zooms in and out of focus over the surface.

In this unique body of work, Salle neutralizes narrative conventions, instead creating a dialogue between art historical references and genres through his incorporation of decorative imagery of furniture, painted images of African masks and Giacometti sculptures, among others. Alive with colliding imagery, the visual cacophony of the Tapestry Paintings emphasizes the primacy of seeing.

Also overt in their stylistic references, Cindy Sherman’s History Portraits take their inspiration from noble historical paintings from the renaissance, baroque, rococo and neo-classical periods. Inspired directly by painted portraits by Raphael, Caravaggio, Ingres and Rubens among others, Sherman uses a range of props and costumes in her classically composed images to play up to the clichés of subjective portraiture.

Throughout her extensive body of work, Sherman has assumed the role of both model and creator of her images. Adopting different styles and personas, she plays upon the stereotypes of women as portrayed in art and propagated in the media. Through her use of props and obvious prosthetic body parts, Sherman draws attention to the performative aspects of her work, thereby calling into question the validity of these male-attributed gender stereotypes.

Invited to collaborate with the French porcelain house Limoges, Sherman made several images, notably Untitled #183 , 1988, loosely based on Madame de Pompadour. Continuing with her research of characters, Sherman created the Citoyennes , Citoyens series, exhibited in Paris in 1989 for the anniversary of the French Revolution. Expanding this theme during a prolonged stay in Rome, Sherman made thirteen portraits based on Renaissance paintings which were exhibited alongside the French series at Metro Pictures, New York in 1990. Sherman eventually made a third series of history portraits drawing inspiration largely from the Renaissance and the seventeenth century.

Evoking the art of painting, Sherman’s re-interpretations are full of theatricality and artifice, calling into question the nature of representation throughout art history and the relationship between painter and model. Intrinsic to each of Sherman’s portraits are their ornate gilded frames, which she designed to emphasize the painterly references in each of the works. The glossy surface and saturated colors of these photographs bring to the fore the artificiality of Sherman’s composition, heightening the theatricality of the performance encased within the frame.

The theme of performance is also central to Salle’s oeuvre. With a long-standing involvement in theatre, Salle has collaborated for over 25 years with choreographer Karole Armitage, creating sets and costumes for her ballets and operas. Pre-dating his seminal Ghost Paintings of 1992, which merge painting, photography and performance, the Tapestry Paintings demonstrate the cross-cultural performative influences on Salle’s work through the incorporation of insert paintings of dancers and photo-transfer images of his own staged photographs. With their juxtaposition of imagery and cultural references, these large-scale paintings are choreographed performances in their own right, their surface a stage for Salle’s ongoing exploration of the performative nature of painting.

In the History Portraits Sherman explores the traditional genre of painting with a multi-layered approach both physically and conceptually. The heavy draped fabrics that form the backdrops of the portraits and the rich, dense coloration of the photographic surface give physical form to her appropriation of this historical genre. Whereas in Salle’s Tapestry Paintings , the layering of numerous citations from across the history of art and design multiplies the number of possible interpretations and offers an alternative notion of authorship.

Positioning these bodies of work in dialogue, the exhibition explores the shared visual strategies and the performative aspects intrinsic to the artists’ work. Created during the same period, the History Portraits and Tapestry Paintings invite us to reflect on the coincidence of the artists’ shared translation of historical sources at this particular moment of contemporary art history and to contemplate the role played by their chosen mediums of painting and photography. The borrowing by Sherman and Salle of visual modes and styles to create a layered pastiche that is original and inventive underlines the success of their artistry, and the continued importance of these historical bodies of work as context for contemporary thought and practice.
